info.title: GigBid API
info.description: Multi-agent freelancer copilot. Every proposal and message waits for a human before it leaves the system.

post.description: Sign in. The reviewer account is seeded from the environment.

get.description: Who the current session belongs to. The UI calls this on load.
The job inbox, ranked by analysed fit first and skill overlap second.
Everything the job detail screen shows, including the evidence matrix.

Every run this user has. Backs the pipeline board and the runs list.

Reads the checkpointer's thread list rather than a separate table, so there is one
source of truth about what has happened and no chance of the two drifting.

post.description:
Register a run and return its thread id. The work happens on the stream.

Idempotent by thread id: starting a run for a job that already has one returns the
existing thread rather than a duplicate, so a double-click cannot produce two threads
bidding on the same job.

get.description: Node-by-node progress over SSE. Starts the run, or resumes watching one.
The run viewer: the trace, node by node, with prompt versions and token counts.

Every thread of this user's that is waiting for a decision.

Queried from the checkpointer rather than an in-memory list, which is what makes a
pending approval survive a restart of this process.
One approval payload: the draft, the evidence behind every claim, risk, price, cost.

post.description:
Approve, edit or reject, and resume the graph.

This is the only path by which anything GigBid produces reaches a client.

get.description: Client threads, with those awaiting approval first.
One conversation, with the drafted reply if the graph has run.

post.description:
Run the conversation graph over this thread, streaming progress.

Ends at an interrupt with a drafted reply, or at `flag_for_user` when the client's
message carries scam signals, in which case no reply is drafted at all.

get.description: The kanban board. Cards move as the marketplace reports outcomes.
Reply and hire rate by category, Connects against outcomes, cost and latency.
What GigBid has learned about this user, and the rule that let each item in.

post.description:
Delete one learned item. Viva question 6 asks for exactly this, from the UI.

By default only the *rule* is deleted, so a later promotion could re-derive it from
the same evidence. `forget_evidence` removes the observations too, which is the
difference between "stop applying this" and "this was never my preference".

get.description: Autonomy, budgets, connected accounts, and what is actually configured.
Is everything the UI depends on actually working?

ApprovalDecisionRequest.title: ApprovalDecisionRequest
ApprovalDecisionRequest.description:
What the approval screen sends back.

`cover_letter` or `text` is required for an edit; the server rejects an edit with no
text rather than sending the original, because that would silently discard the
human's change.

forget_evidence.title: Forget Evidence
forget_evidence.description: Also delete the observations, so promotion cannot re-derive the rule.

degraded.title: Degraded
degraded.description: Subsystems that are down. The UI shows a banner per entry.

JobDetail.title: JobDetail
JobDetail.description: The job detail screen: spec, risk, the requirement-to-evidence matrix, price.

JobSummary.title: JobSummary
JobSummary.description: A row in the job inbox, ranked by fit.

MemoryView.title: MemoryView
MemoryView.description: The settings screen's memory viewer: what was learned, why, and how to delete it.

payload.title: Payload
payload.description: Everything the human needs: draft, evidence per claim, risk, price, the dry-run preview and its cost.

token.title: Token
token.description: Also set as an HttpOnly cookie.

persona.title: Persona
persona.description: Defaults to the signed-in user's persona.

retry.title: Retry
retry.description: Start a fresh thread when the previous attempt ended in needs_attention.
